title: 2025 AMC 12A Problem 1
statement: Andy and Betsy both live in Mathville. Andy leaves Mathville on his bicycle at \(1{:}30,\) traveling due north at a steady \(8\) miles per hour. Betsy leaves on her bicycle from the same point at \(2{:}30,\) traveling due east at a steady \(12\) miles per hour. At what time will they be exactly the same distance from their common starting point?

solutions.text:
Let \(t\) be the number of hours since \(1{:}30.\) Andy has traveled \(8t\) miles north, and Betsy, who started an hour later, has traveled \(12(t-1)\) miles east.

Setting the distances equal, \[8t = 12(t-1),\] so \(4t = 12\) and \(t = 3.\)

Three hours after \(1{:}30\) is \(4{:}30.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Measure time from \(1{:}30\); Betsy has been riding one hour less than Andy
If Andy has ridden \(t\) hours, set \(8t = 12(t-1)\)
